html:
The Straits Settlements were Britain's ports of Penang, Malacca and Singapore, joined into one territory in 1826. Singapore became the capital in 1832, and in 1867 they became a crown colony.

They were free ports, open to traders of all nations, and became the gateway for British influence into the Malay states. Chinese and Indian migrants made up most of their people.

The settlements were run from Singapore until the Second World War. In 1946 Britain broke them up: Penang and Malacca joined the Malayan Union, while Singapore became a separate colony. See also Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824.
